data.originalIdea: How to write code that other developers can actually read
How to write code that other developers can actually read

data.instruction: Giọng điệu: người thợ đang chỉ trχει một sai lầm phổ biến — mỗi câu ngắn, gắt, kết bằng meta so sánh (clock/breath). Beat 1 là câu hỏi tu từ, beat 2 vạch ra gốc rễ vấn đề, beat 3 đưa ra quy tắc dùng được ngay.
data.idea: Readable code is a gift to your future self

beats.transcript: Code that works but nobody can read is technical debt you pay every single day.
Naming is the cheapest refactor. A good function name replaces three lines of comments.
Small functions are not about line count. They are about one idea per unit.
Comments explain WHY, never WHAT. If your comment describes the code, rewrite the code.
Consistency beats correctness. A codebase that does the same thing the same way everywhere is readable even when it is wrong.
The test is simple: can someone new to the codebase find what they need in under thirty seconds?
Write code as if the person maintaining it is a violent psychopath who knows where you live. That person is you, six months from now.
